subject: Model catalog: licensing, provenance, pinning & escrow — Atlas Health RFP
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas RFP — Model catalog licensing / pinning questionnaire

Soojin,

Thanks for taking part in Atlas Health's vendor RFP. Attached is the model catalog licensing & provenance worksheet we use to assess suppliers (atlas_rfi_questions_v1.xlsx). Our security and procurement teams need clarifications on the following so we can advance to the legal stage:  

- For each model in your hosted catalog, specify the open-source license used (or commercial license if applicable) and the exact source artifact/commit/hash you can attest to.
- Describe your version pinning semantics: can customers pin a model artifact to an immutable SHA/commit? How do you expose pinning options in hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment?
- Update cadence and notification: what is your policy for model updates (patch, minor, major)? Do you provide a changelog + SBOM for each update?
- Rollback and emergency rollback: what controls exist to return to a prior pinned artifact? Are there guarantees for backward compatibility?
- Escrow / provenance evidence: what artifacts do you provide for audit (SBOM, model weights provenance, licensing attestations)? Do you support escrow for high-compliance customers?

We also have a couple of must-haves for finalist vendors: 1) a formal pinning playbook or policy document; 2) evidence of provenance for at least one open-source model in your catalog; 3) a draft addendum for model updates in enterprise SLAs.  

Can you respond by EOD Thursday 9/30 with the completed worksheet and a short summary? If you prefer a short tech call for the provenance questions, mark availability and we'll book.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager, Atlas Health
Samantha.Lee@atlashealth.com
+1 415-555-0188

Attachment: atlas_rfi_questions_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet of questionnaire)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas RFP — Model catalog licensing / pinning questionnaire

Samantha —

Thanks for the worksheet and clear asks. We've completed the questionnaire and attached our answers (redwood_atlas_rfi_answers_v1.pdf). High-level summary up front to save your team time:  

- Licensing: Each catalog entry includes license metadata (OSI/SPDX identifiers when available). We include the original model repository URL + artifact checksum and our verified copy hash. For commercial models we provide contract references.

- Pinning: Customers can pin to an immutable artifact ID (SHA256) on all deployment modes. Hosted API offers "pin-by-model-id:sha" in request headers for per-call pinning; Dedicated and Private allow tenant-level and route-level pin policies. Pinning is enforced at the runtime/serving layer and recorded in audit logs.

- Updates: We classify updates as patch/minor/major. Customers are notified 14 days in advance for minor changes and 45 days for major changes; emergency security fixes can be deployed with immediate notifications and optional forced rollback windows. Changelogs + SBOMs are published per model version.

- Rollback & compatibility: Our serving runtime supports atomic rollbacks to a pinned artifact; we retain prior artifacts for a customer-configured retention window (default 90 days). We do not guarantee semantic compatibility across major-version upgrades — we recommend pin-and-evaluate for major changes.

- Escrow / provenance: For enterprise customers we provide a provenance bundle (source repo snapshot, build recipe, artifact hashes, licensing attestation). Escrow arrangements can be made for long-term archival — we work with your legal to define scope.

Per your must-haves: we've attached the completed worksheet and an internal pinning playbook extract. Marissa (product) is copied for any catalog or SBOM questions; Jordan (legal) is copied for escrow/addendum language. If it's helpful we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through this Thursday or Friday.

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_atlas_rfi_answers_v1.pdf (PDF — completed questionnaire + annotated evidence)

Thanks Soojin — that summary is helpful. A few follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the PDF:  

1) For the "provenance bundle" you mention, can you confirm the exact files included and whether those files include build logs and the toolchain versions used to produce the weights? Our auditors require reproducible build records.

2) On pinning enforcement: what prevents a tenant admin from accidentally unpinning (or a misconfigured rollout from changing route-level pin policies)? Is there a guardrail / review step?

3) We need explicit retention windows for retained artifacts in hosted mode — can you state a default retention and whether retention can be set to "indefinite" under an enterprise contract/escrow?

4) For SLA addendum: can you provide (a) a sample update-notice clause; (b) a remediation/rollback timeline for critical regressions; (c) a pricing mechanism if we choose to require model escrow (i.e., one-time escrow fee vs ongoing storage)?

We'd like the provenance tech call — Thu 9/30 at 11:00 AM PT works for our engineers. Please include anyone who can speak to build reproducibility and runtime enforcement.

Cheers,
Samantha

Subject: Re: Atlas RFP — Model catalog licensing / pinning questionnaire (follow-ups + call agenda)

Samantha —

Great — we've booked Thu 9/30 11:00 AM PT for the provenance deep-dive (calendar invite sent). Below are concise answers to your security team's follow-ups and the call agenda. If you'd like these copied into an addendum draft we can have Jordan produce language after the call.

1) Provenance bundle contents (what we deliver):
- source_snapshot.tar.gz (repository snapshot at commit referenced, includes commit hash and tag)
- build_manifest.json (toolchain versions, pip/conda/nixpkgs refs, build commands, and language/runtime versions)
- build_logs.tar.gz (timestamped build logs for the artifact creation)
- model_weights.sha256 (checksums for weight files)
- license_attestation.pdf (signed by Redwood legal with SPDX mapping)
Notes: build manifests include explicit container images or Bazel/Nix derivations when available; for third-party models we include upstream commit + our build steps.

2) Pinning guardrails and enforcement:
- Role-based safeguards: Only tenant admins or users with a pinned-role can change tenant-level pin policies. Route-level pins require a two-step confirmation in the console + an audit reason.
- Approval/workflow integrations: We provide an API hook for external approval systems (e.g., your change management) and can require a 24-hour approval hold by default for tenant-wide unpins.
- Immutable ledger: All pin changes generate an audit event with before/after artifact hashes and changed-by metadata; events are retained per contract retention windows.

3) Retention & escrow options: 
- Hosted default: 90 days of retained prior artifacts/weights (configurable).
- Enterprise option: retention can be extended to customer-specified windows, including indefinite archival via escrow. Escrow options: one-time archival fee (covers retrieval/verification) or an annual storage/maintenance fee — Jordan can provide sample pricing tiers.

4) SLA addendum (draft points):
- Update-notice: 14 days for minor, 45 days for major; emergency security updates with immediate notification and rollback window.
- Critical regression remediation: Redwood will execute a rollback to most-recent-pinned artifact within 2 hours of verified critical regression and notify within 30 minutes of detection.
- Escrow pricing: sample language to be provided; typical approach is a one-time ingestion + verification fee plus annual storage and compliance verification fee.

Call agenda (30 min):
- 5m intro & goals (Samantha + Soojin)
- 10m provenance bundle walkthrough (Marissa)
- 10m pinning enforcement & audit logs (SoJin + Eng lead)
- 5m next steps & addendum timeline (Jordan)

Attachments: pinning_playbook_v1.2.pdf (high-level playbook + API examples), redwood_atlas_rfi_answers_v1.pdf

If that all looks good I'll follow up with a draft addendum and sample escrow pricing. Looking forward to the call.

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
